newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's car incentive scheme help sales in south.
newsitem.headline: Italy's car incentive scheme help sales in south.

text.p: Italy's new car incentive buying scheme is helping boost car sales in the nation's poor south more than in its richer northern regions, Italy's car importers association Unrae said on Tuesday.

New car registrations in the region of Campania, in southern Italy around Naples, represented 4.73 percent of all new car sales in Italy during May 1997, up from 3.61 percent in the same month of 1996, an Unrae statement said.
It added that the region of Lombardy in the north of Italy saw its share of new car sales fall to 20.06 percent in May 1997 from 21.58 percent in May 1996.
Earlier today, the Italian Ministry of Transport released data showing Italian new car registrations in May up 43.23 percent at 232,600 compared to May 1996.

In the January-May period of 1997, new car sales in Italy's north-east were 34.51 percent of total sales from 35.58 percent in the same period in 1996. In Italy's north west sales were 24.31 percent in May after 25.07 percent, while central regions accounted for 23.64 percent after 23.76 percent, and the south and islands 17.54 percent from 15.60 percent.

Italy's new car incentive scheme financed by the government and the car industry started in early January and offers owners of cars over 10 year old price discount if they trade them in for new cars. The scheme is set to run until end-September.
